verdict.notes: Static source grading only; no test execution claimed. Main reviewed-object mutation is accurately demonstrated. None reports supplier-note recognition or fully resolves configured factories, session binding and host lifetime. Code-only authority is sufficient; no external semantics/provenance verification asserted. Read-history statements cannot be independently authenticated. Conditional functional/redesign/hardening proposals are allowed, not presumed tested drop-in patches. No deployment/release conclusion or served-identity inference. Errors: reapproval called repeated delivery on one approval; unknown-tool probing called traceless despite host journal; per-item resolve and expiry behavior misstated; double-execute test wrongly expected to fail, with whole suite called happy-only. Plans.digest class typo is noted but not counted as independent finding error.
unsupported_gap_claims: Anyone with `approve` can re-review a plan that has already run, and the owner can then execute it again. That gives repeated deliveries on a single approval. — New authorized review is a new approval. Per-decision consume rejects a second execution; assertion of single-approval repeated deliveries is false. This also covers closing claim that #1/#2 together let it run repeatedly without naming new reviewer action.

Probing and failed auth attempts therefore leave no trace. — Overbroad no-trace assertion: valid-session unknown-tool probes are caught and journaled failed by host, explicitly in test. Failed auth and malformed pre-try errors are narrower actual trace gaps.

The first `resolve` also isn't repeated per call, so a session that expires mid-batch is handled per item. — invoke explicitly repeats resolve for every item; expiry then raises outside try and aborts whole batch, rather than returning item error.

The tests cover only the happy path. Nothing tests update-after-review, double execute, re-review after consume, cross-tenant access or self-approval. The first two would fail today. — Named missing tests are real, but whole suite has negative input/credential/tool tests. More materially double-execute denial would pass current consumed guard, not fail. Grouped test-expectation/inventory error.
